rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all eight compounds and identify critical separations while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained components. The moderate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity changes in the crowded middle cluster and final pair. All peaks currently elute well before 10 minutes, leaving time for a shallower gradient if needed.
Test the low-temperature selectivity limit with the gradient unchanged. This will show whether cooling separates the crowded middle peaks and avoids the near-coelution observed at 60 C.

Cooling gave the best selectivity, so retain 25 C and make the gradient shallower to improve the two remaining critical pairs. The current last peak at 6.92 minutes leaves room to gain resolution before the time penalty becomes substantial.
Raise the starting organic fraction to bring the last peak below 10 minutes while slightly reducing the gradient slope. The shallower slope may lift the remaining critical pair from R 1.47 above 1.5.

Lengthen the best sub-10-minute gradient by one grid step to improve the sole unresolved pair. The last peak is expected near 10 minutes, making this a promising route to full resolution with little or no time penalty.

The maximum CRF is achieved; now raise the starting organic fraction one step to seek a shorter fully resolved method. Keep 25 C and the 22-minute gradient to preserve the favorable selectivity and resolution margin.

Raise the starting organic fraction one more step to test whether elution can be shortened further without losing full resolution. Injection 7 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback, since its critical pair has little margin at R 1.52.

Retain the faster starting composition but use a shallower gradient to recover resolution of the sole critical pair. This tests whether full resolution can be restored with the last peak still earlier than injection 7's 8.90 minutes.

Test a one-step temperature increase from the fastest fully resolved method to shorten retention and measure its effect on the critical pair. Injection 7 remains the fallback if warming reduces resolution below 1.5.

Combine the higher starting organic fraction, which improved spacing ahead of the middle cluster at 25 C, with the modest warming that improved its other critical gap. The 26-minute gradient may provide enough resolution while keeping the last peak earlier than the current fully resolved method.

Lengthen the gradient one step to lift the middle critical pair above R 1.5 while retaining the shorter elution window achieved at 30 C. Monitor the final pair closely because its current R 1.65 leaves only a small margin.

Test whether another temperature step separates the final pair after an elution-order reversal while preserving the middle separations. The maximum-score method is already secured, so this probes a potentially faster selectivity regime.

Return to the favorable 25 C selectivity and test a substantially higher starting organic fraction for faster elution. The middle pair converged as phi0 increased, so this probes whether separation recovers beyond an elution-order reversal.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step from the new fastest fully resolved method to shorten elution further. Check whether compression of the early peaks or middle cluster consumes the available resolution margin.

Back off to the fully resolved starting composition and shorten the gradient to accelerate the late peaks. This tests how much of injection 14's resolution margin can be traded for a shorter separation.

Shorten the gradient further while retaining the successful starting composition and temperature. The smallest resolution is still 1.91, suggesting room to accelerate elution before a critical pair falls below 1.5.
Shorten the gradient by one grid step to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary at 25 C. Injection 17 remains the fallback if either of its two marginal pairs falls below R 1.5.

Return to the shortest fully resolved gradient and raise temperature one step to test whether faster elution can preserve full resolution. This probes temperature selectivity in the higher-starting-organic regime, where peak spacing differs substantially from the earlier temperature trials.

Probe higher-temperature selectivity beyond the middle-pair convergence seen at 30 C, seeking separation after an elution-order reversal. Injection 17 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback while this tests a potentially shorter regime.

Return to 25 C and lower the starting organic fraction to improve the middle-pair selectivity, while shortening the gradient to offset the added retention. This tests a nearby route to a faster fully resolved separation than injection 17.

Test whether warming the higher-starting-organic method separates its critical middle pair after an elution-order reversal. Injection 17 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback; this trial seeks a shorter separation through temperature-dependent selectivity.

Refine the gradient slope between the fully resolved injection 17 and the slightly too-steep injection 18 by lowering the endpoint to 0.90. This tests for a shorter maximum-score separation while retaining the proven starting composition and temperature.

Preserve injection 17's successful gradient slope but end the programmed gradient earlier at 0.55 organic. Its outlet endpoint at 4.65 minutes is later than the observed last peak at 4.14 minutes, so this should retain full resolution with a shorter gradient program.

Test the minimum gradient duration while preserving the successful initial slope, then hold at 0.45 organic to elute the remaining peaks. This may retain maximum CRF with a shorter gradient program, although late elution could lengthen; injection 24 remains the fully resolved fallback.
